thread:
matt (infra): Heads up — saw a big latency spike during the nightly epoch run on rack-23 around 03:10 UTC. Throughput down ~40% for multi-gpu jobs. Ops-bot fired an alert.
ops-bot: [ALERT] nvlink_link_error threshold breached on node gpu-rack23-07. PCIe AER events: 3, Xid errors detected.
matt (infra): quick dmesg excerpt:
```
[03:10:12] nvidia 0000:81:00.0: AER: Corrected error, enabled
[03:10:14] nvlink-0: link 0 flapping: up->down->up
[03:10:16] GPU 3: Xid (31) Display driver stopped responding
```
julia (sre): ugh. ECC counters?
matt (infra): ECC SBE on GPU3 rising: `nvidia-smi -q -d ECC` shows SBE 124 -> 210 over 2h. Also seeing `Uncorrected` PCIe AER increments for 81:00.0.
kevin (mlops): Can we repro on another node first? Suggest drain and move jobs off, then run a controlled multi-gpu job. `kubectl drain gpu-rack23-07 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` then repro.
sophie (eng): If NVLink flaps, multi-gpu KV cache can get invalidated which explains the severe perf hit. Fallback to single-GPU model until we confirm.
julia (sre): Proposed triage steps (short): 1) cordon/evict node; 2) collect `dmesg`, `lspci -vvv`, `nvidia-bug-report.sh`; 3) power-cycle GPU/riser; 4) if persists, RMA.
matt (infra): cordoning now. Also noting bus resets: `PCIe Bus Reset` seen in logs ~03:11. Could be riser/cable/slot.
kevin (mlops): I'll migrate the active epoch to gpu-rack23-09 and re-run to check whether it's rack-local. If that runs fine, we avoid noisy global rollback.
sophie (eng): For monitoring: add NVLink link-state and GPU ECC rate to console dashboards. Also track KV cache miss rate so we can correlate perf drops to link flaps.
matt (infra): ops update: cordoned and drained. Running `nvidia-bug-report.sh` now; uploading logs when done. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: [ACTION] Node gpu-rack23-07 cordoned by matt (infra) at 03:25 UTC
matt (infra): pasted short log snippet -> `/var/log/nvlink/gpu3-03-10.log` excerpt: `link state change: lane 2 timeout` + repeated `AER: Uncorrected` entries. Power-cycled the node, quick smoke shows link came up then flapped again during a 30m run.
julia (sre): power-cycle transient suggests thermal/connector or riser fatigue. If flapping returns after cycle, schedule RMA for the card or riser. Keep thermal and current draw numbers.
kevin (mlops): FYI cost impact: had to move some jobs to single-gpu instances and spin up extra spot capacity — estimated +12% infra spend next 24h if this drags.
sophie (eng): note for postmortem: add an alert for NVLink flap rate (lower threshold) and playbook step to shift multi-gpu to single-gpu fallback automatically.
matt (infra): will follow up with full logs + `lspci` dump. If RMA goes through we'll swap GPU3 and test on bench before returning to prod.
julia (sre): thanks. please tag me when you have the bug-report upload so I can update the incident ticket.
